extraction_metadata.notes: DeepHealth (a RadNet company) received FDA 510(k) clearance on September 16, 2026 for DeepHealth Chest XRay, a CADe solution built on a proprietary chest X-ray foundation model. This is the first wave of foundation-model-based regulatory clearances — exactly the certification regime OSIRIS's Theorem 7 formalizes.

title: DeepHealth Chest XRay receives FDA 510(k) clearance — a foundation model crosses the regulatory threshold
subtitle_or_tagline: CADe built on a chest X-ray foundation model covers nodules, consolidation and more
topic: On September 16, 2026 DeepHealth announced FDA 510(k) clearance for its chest X-ray CADe solution built on a proprietary foundation model, covering detection of nodules, consolidation, and additional findings. This marks the transition of foundation-model architectures from research demos to regulated medical devices. The clearance answers the question the whole field has been asking: can a large pretrained model, rather than a narrow task-specific network, meet the FDA's safety and effectiveness bar?

Step 2 - Adapt CADe head for localized finding detection
Step 3 - Validate performance against regulatory benchmarks

key_claims: Built on a proprietary chest X-ray foundation model (not a narrow task-specific network)
Covers nodules, consolidation, and additional findings
CADe classification: detection is intended to flag findings for radiologist review
Signals that regulators will accept foundation-model architectures when evidence is sufficient
caveats_or_warnings: 510(k) clearance is substantial equivalence, not a proof of generalization beyond the predicate domain
CADe output requires radiologist confirmation — the device assists, it does not replace
Foundation-model drift under distribution shift remains an open regulatory question
osiris_connection: The FDA 510(k) is a procedural certificate: it bounds behavior by evidence of substantial equivalence, not by mathematics. OSIRIS's interpretability-vs-certification theorem card argues the complement — a mathematical bound (Theorem 7: displacement <= L*c) is the formal analog of what the FDA approximates procedurally. DeepHealth's clearance shows the regulatory pathway works for foundation models; OSIRIS shows what the mathematical version of that certificate should look like. The gap between 'cleared' and 'certified' is exactly the platform's reason to exist.
